lines.speaker: Rosa
lines.text: What we know is that thirty-six places are booked across four dates: eight, ten, nine and nine. Each date has two employees who confirmed it directly.

lines.speaker: Malik
lines.text: We also know that five hundred and twenty dollars is committed and twelve extra staff-hours are scheduled. That leaves a maximum margin of two hundred and eighty dollars and eight hours.

lines.speaker: Rosa
lines.text: The most likely scenario is that all four evenings run within the framework, because every current booking fits the menu, capacity and staffing rules.

lines.speaker: Malik
lines.text: I agree that it is the baseline, but “most likely” does not mean guaranteed. A late cancellation or illness could still change one date.

lines.speaker: Rosa
lines.text: There’s a reasonable chance that one evening needs a small adjustment. Two groups asked whether they could reduce their final number up to forty-eight hours before service.

lines.speaker: Malik
lines.text: If a group reduces its number before the food-order cutoff, Rosa will update the order and the event can continue. If it happens later, some food cost may remain.

lines.speaker: Rosa
lines.text: The evidence suggests that a minor booking change is more plausible than a full cancellation, but four dates are still a very small sample.

lines.speaker: Malik
lines.text: We can rule out accepting more than twelve people under this framework. We can’t rule out a group asking, so the reply template needs to state the limit.

lines.speaker: Rosa
lines.text: A staffing failure is possible, but not especially likely, because every date currently has two confirmations and one optional backup contact.

lines.speaker: Malik
lines.text: Be careful with “backup.” That person agreed to receive a call, not to work automatically. If one confirmed employee withdraws, the date pauses unless another person accepts it directly.

lines.speaker: Rosa
lines.text: The least likely scenario is that several problems occur together and threaten both the cost and hour ceilings.

lines.speaker: Malik
lines.text: It may be the least likely, but it has the highest impact. If extra cleanup, food waste and a late staffing change combine, the remaining margin could disappear quickly.

lines.speaker: Rosa
lines.text: The risk increases if we add off-menu requests or treat a late cancellation as a reason to extend the event. Neither action is allowed.

lines.speaker: Malik
lines.text: And if projected spending reaches eight hundred dollars or projected hours reach twenty, the next event will be paused before the limit is crossed.

lines.speaker: Rosa
lines.text: How likely is that under the current bookings? I’d call it unlikely, based on committed costs and scheduled hours, but not impossible.

lines.speaker: Malik
lines.text: That is defensible. What we don’t know yet is the actual cleanup time, final attendance or whether the three-item menu prevents last-minute preparation.

lines.speaker: Rosa
lines.text: Then the safest conclusion is that the framework has enough recorded margin to begin, provided that every gate remains active.

lines.speaker: Malik
lines.text: Yes. The briefing should not say the trial is low-risk overall. It should say which scenario is more likely, which one matters most and what triggers a pause.

lines.speaker: Rosa
lines.text: I’ll list a baseline, an adjustment scenario and a combined-pressure scenario, with evidence and actions beside each one.

lines.speaker: Malik
lines.text: Good. After the second evening, we’ll replace these estimates with recorded cost, time, attendance and recovery evidence before continuing.
